text:
anya: kicking off a traffic dry-run for the new-llama-xl variants — int4-awq, fp8, and gptq. plan: sampled traffic 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% over 45m windows, hosted + dedicated. primary checks: rouge / pass@k deltas, p95 latency, error spike detection. posting baseline numbers in a bit. ping @sasha for infra knobs and @devon for alerting.

sasha: SGTM. i will set a soft cpu/gpu autoscale buffer and enable node draining ramp. will also make sure the dedicated pools have fallback pool mapping.

devon: adding two temporary alerts: (1) 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained 3m, (2) p95 latency increase > 30% vs baseline. ops runbook mapped to the thread.

jess: product note — include the safety-eval set (policy triggers + hallucination tests). if delta > 1.5% on safety triggers we stop.

anya: summary of quick evals on held-out evalset (small sample):
```
baseline fp16 -> rougeL: 42.8, p95: 210ms
int4-awq -> rougeL: 42.1 (-0.7), p95: 190ms
fp8 -> rougeL: 42.5 (-0.3), p95: 200ms
gptq -> rougeL: 41.9 (-0.9), p95: 175ms
```
notes: int4 looks promising on latency but has a ~0.7-0.9 drop on this set. fp8 is almost neutral. gptq best latency but slightly larger quality delta.

leo: quick question — are we routing by model variant or by compiled-kernel family? need to know fallback compat matrix.

sasha: routing policy: variant-aware routing at request-time. fallback order configured: fp16 -> fp8 -> int4-awq -> gptq-approx. We also have a compatibility mapping so older clients can fallback to fp16.

anya: running the first 0.5% window now. logs stream: `/tools/replay --model new-llama-xl --variants int4,fp8,gptq --percent 0.5 --duration 15m`

ci-bot: perf-run completed for int4-awq sample: avg_latency=155ms p95=185ms tokens/sec=4200; summary uploaded to /artifacts/1963012345/perf.json

devon: alert threshold watchers armed. i'll be online for the next 90m. if anything trips, mark with :rotating_light: and i'll cut traffic.

anya: first 15m window results (0.5%):
- int4-awq: delta rougeL -0.6, policy-triggers +0.4% (within limit), errors +0.02%
- fp8: delta rougeL -0.2, policy-triggers 0.0%, errors 0.01%
- gptq: delta rougeL -0.8, policy-triggers +0.7% (just below stop threshold)

jess: safety-eval pass for fp8 and int4 (sample), gptq has a slight uptick on hallucination heuristic — can we run the targeted eval set?

anya: running targeted safety suite now (estimate 8m).

ci-bot: safety-run finished. results link: /artifacts/1963012345/safety.json

anya: safety-suite results:
- int4-awq: safety triggers +0.3% (ok)
- fp8: +0.1% (ok)
- gptq: +1.9% (exceeds product stop threshold of 1.5%)

sasha: recommendation: hold gptq in warm pool, do not promote. continue fp8 -> staged -> 1% traffic. int4: promote carefully to 1% with stricter rollback window.

devon: agreed. rolling int4 to 1% now, fp8 to 1% in parallel. will keep gptq at 0% active routing.

anya: note to logs: annotate model-config with `quant-run:1963012345` and `traffic-plan:0.5-1-5`.

leo: can we capture per-route token-economics? i'd like cost/token delta for each variant (rough ballpark).

anya: early estimate tokens-cost delta: int4 ~ -37% cost, fp8 ~ -22%, gptq ~ -40% (but quality regs). will produce a small report.

jess: product decision: proceed with fp8 staged rollout to 5% after the next 15m if safety stays green. int4 needs a longer evaluation and an expanded evalset for coverage. gptq needs model-side calibration work.

devon: moving autoscale back to baseline after 45m window unless we see anomalies.

anya: thanks all. i'll open a short follow-up doc with the perf + safety artifacts and the recommended rollout policy (fp8: staged to 5% in 30m, int4: extended 1% 2h runway, gptq: hold & calibrate). tagging this thread in the rollout ticket. :white_check_mark:
